mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate above 8% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 8% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower (t-test p > 0.05) when UNRATE exceeds 8% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and lowers profit expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO falls for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous and persistent decline in both the federal funds rate and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) over three months signals a deflationary monetary easing, which depresses risk-free rates and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both decline for three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL decline for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive correlation between personal income (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) over a six-month window indicates robust household formation and spending, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher (t-test p > 0.05) when the correlation between PAYEMS and HOUST exceeds 0.7 for six months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 2% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as earnings growth offsets cost pressures.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS grows > 2% month-over-month for three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher (t-test p > 0.05) when PAYEMS grows above 2% month-over-month for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) over four consecutive months, despite rising disposable income (implied by PAYEMS), indicates precautionary behavior by households, which reduces near-term consumption and corporate revenue, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where RSAFS rises for four consecutive months.
